anchors.boundary: Original Bell publication + NIST + independent history bind control-chart origin/process logic; exact causal share of statistical method versus management/metrology in early productivity is not quantified.
Smithsonian material/archive plus Library of Congress bind tube/network diffusion; precise patent-pool economic contribution versus receiver/content demand remains unresolved.

IEEE, Imperial War Museums and Science Museum independently bind Chain Home system and magnetron transition; exact marginal causal share of radar versus Dowding organization/fighter force remains unresolved.
Nobel, AIP and APS histories bind competing formalisms/predictive convergence; this anchor must not settle the interpretation/ontology of quantum mechanics.

DOE owner history plus Nobel Fermi lineage bind pre-fission neutron work, CP-1 and production transition; wartime secrecy means fine-grained cost/schedule attribution among parallel industrial routes remains incomplete.

NIDDK history and independent medical-history work bind treatment/purification/standardization trajectory; exact contributor priority and early access-versus-pharmacology mortality decomposition remain unresolved.
Two independent peer-reviewed historical syntheses bind Fleming→Oxford→US production; exact quantitative contribution of strain/media/deep-tank changes is not isolated.

NASA/NACA primary technical reports plus independent Smithsonian history bind scaling, cowling and full-scale instrumentation; industrial adoption share versus propulsion/manufacturing remains unresolved.
GCHQ owner history plus Computer History Museum bind Polish/British/U.S. machine lineages; secrecy and retrospective first-computer narratives prevent a single priority verdict.
NASA owner history plus Smithsonian material/archive bind Goddard local experiments and later system gap; direct influence versus independent German reinvention remains unresolved.
ACS industrial history plus Nobel Staudinger lineage bind macromolecule theory and polymer scale; wartime GR-S route-specific cost/performance decomposition remains partial.

USDA ARS/NASS evidence plus independent Smithsonian history bind hybridization/search/adoption; yield gains cannot be cleanly decomposed from weather, agronomy and mechanization using this anchor alone.

schemaAudit.finding: Statistical process control, wartime networks, predictive-formalism plurality, nuclear/bioprocess scale-up, human-machine computation, rocketry, polymer science and agricultural search all remain representable with the existing trajectory schema. New pressure concerns decision-world urgency, secrecy, scale and evidence validity rather than missing historical ontology.

sourceBoundary: Source lock supports trajectory reconstruction, not exhaustive priority/cost attribution. War-era secrecy and institutional archives are especially likely to preserve uneven evidence; unknowns are retained rather than normalized away.
